key_insight: RheOFormer’s failures in steady Bingham channel flow can be mitigated with logarithmic velocity representations, gradient-aware losses, and a few strategically selected training cases.
engineering_relevance: These remedies support more reliable, data-efficient viscoplastic-flow surrogates, especially where low-gradient plug regions challenge prediction.
method: Evaluate RheOFormer interpolation and extrapolation across dataset structures, value ranges, and input representations.
Introduce logarithmic velocity representations and gradient-aware losses to improve plug-region predictions.
Augment training with cases covering missing physical regimes and predict steady flow from a partially developed snapshot.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved accuracy in challenging regimes, reduced extrapolation error with a few added cases, and single-snapshot predictions that outperform copying the input throughout flow development.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to steady Bingham channel flow; transfer to complex geometries or other constitutive models remains unestablished.
paper_title: Failure Modes and Data-Efficient Remedies for Transformer-Based Prediction of Viscoplastic Flows
